verdicts.reasons:
Blocking reasons:
1. The section row has position: relative, so it paints over the top 4 px of Change's hit box. A press 1 px inside Change's top edge folds the band instead of opening Shared defaults. Presses 2 px and 5 px above Change also fold it. This happens at all four widths. On d04 the same presses do nothing.
2. The empty-key truth gap (see AT02) applies here too.

Other costs:
- The open band is 24 px taller at every width (130 vs 106 at 373; 241 vs 217 at 160), and open is the state every first open shows.
- At 189 and 160 px, one row holds only Change, because the hidden label leaves its grid cell empty.
- When the themes payload arrives after the fold answer, the folded row grows from 31 to 35 px, a 4 px shift.

Strengths: it is the only variant whose row matches the other section titles, and it answers 'what is drawn and where from' both open and folded.

My A2 trial raises Change (position: relative; z-index: 1) and adds a 6 px gap under the row. Every miss then does nothing except a press 5 px above, at a further +6 px of height. That is the fallback if the owner weighs 'like the other sections' over height.

required_changes.change:
In proto-B.css (and in production pi.css), while the band is open, end the fold row's box 8 px before Change instead of padding the row under it:
`details.hw-look-fold[open] > summary.hw-look-name { margin-right: 64px; padding-right: 8px; }`

This replaces the open-state `padding-right: 72px`. 64 px is Change's width (44.5 px) plus the 12 px gutter plus an 8 px dead gap. The name keeps exactly the same width.

The folded row keeps `padding-right: var(--hw-gutter)` and runs full width, because Change is not rendered when the band is folded.

On hover, the row's highlight now ends before Change. That correctly shows Change as its own target.
required_changes.why: On B and C, a press that misses Change by 2 to 6 px folds the band. That fold is a remembered view preference, so it then holds on every panel of that kind. d04 ignores those presses. The d04 design deliberately gave Change 'its whole hit area' (the pi-common.js comment).
required_changes.acceptance_test:
Setup: a Default key with the band open, at 373x410 and 320x410 (DPR 1.5) and at 189x205 and 160x205 (DPR 3).

1. Real mouse presses 2 px above, 2 px and 5 px below, and 2 px and 6 px left and right of #theme-change leave #sec-theme open, leave scrollY unchanged and leave #sec-shared closed.
2. A press 1 px inside Change's top edge still opens Shared defaults.
3. The open band height stays 113 px at 373 and 233 px at 160.
4. No horizontal overflow.

Passed on hw-tf-adversarial/proto-B2 with lab6.mjs and lab1.mjs.

answers.q1_variant:
B, with AT01 and AT02 (both blocking), then AT03 to AT05.

Open: B's fold row is today's line ('Theme Default (shared: Void)' plus Change) with a fold marker. What is drawn (the bold name above the named chips, with the checked chip ringed) and where it comes from ('shared: Void' or 'set on this key') read exactly as on d04, for +7 px of height.

Folded: 'Theme [chip] (shared: Void)' keeps the palette, the name on the chip face, Default's link mark and dashed frame, and the scope. MEASURED at 373, 320, 189 and 160 with a Default key, an explicit Paper theme, a Paper shared theme and an Ultraviolet dial.

It fails in two places today:
- A key with no reading, folded, claims a palette the key does not draw (fixed by AT02).
- A press that misses Change by 2 to 6 px folds the band (fixed by AT01).

Fallback, if the owner weighs 'like the other sections' over height: A, with Change raised above the row and a 6 px gap (A2, +30 px open against d04), plus AT02. Reject C: B dominates it.
answers.q2_fold_all:
Yes, include the band, as all three prototypes already do through the shell's details.hw-sec[id] selector.

MEASURED:
- Fold all folds the band and the row keeps the chip and scope (A, B, C).
- The fold bar's aria-disabled states stay truthful: with only the theme open, Fold all stays offered.
- Alt-click on the theme row folds everything.
- The fold is remembered on the next key.

So Fold all does not hide the only visual of the theme: the folded chip and the header's live face both stay on screen.

Excluding the band would need a special case in setAllFolds and syncFoldBar, a new rule the owner said not to add. It would also leave the tallest band (106 to 130 px) open in the most compact view.

Note for the owner: fold memory is per panel kind, so a key's fold does not reach dial panels (MEASURED).
answers.q3_hidden_until_answer:
Acceptable. The claim that hiding the band hides the palette on every panel open is refuted.

The chips cannot draw before the plugin's themes payload arrives, and that payload travels on the same plugin round trip as the fold answer. MEASURED with 250 ms reply latency:
- d04 draws its first chips at 284 to 308 ms.
- B shows its band with chips at 285 to 301 ms.
- C shows it at 277 to 284 ms.

Before that, d04 shows only the word 'Theme' (38 px), then pushes the page down 68 px when the chips land.

With the themes payload held 900 ms after the fold answer:
- B and C folded rows keep their height (33 and 41 px) and fill in place.
- A grows from 31 to 35 px, a 4 px shift.

The 300 ms cap after connect and the 1.5 s overall cap apply as for every section. The rule that turns off the marker transition while folds are pending also covers the theme row (READ pi.css).
answers.q4_accessibility:
The fold row must be a native summary (APG Disclosure pattern). That gives it a disclosure role, an expanded or collapsed state, and a name made of its visible words (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name). Examples:
- 'Theme Default (shared: Void)'
- 'Theme Paper (set on this key)'
- 'Theme "neon" (unknown; draws Void)'
- with AT02, on an empty key: '... Shows on the key once a reading is picked.'

MEASURED with CDP accessibility nodes:
- B and C give the same name open and folded.
- A gives 'Theme' open and the full line folded.
- The doubled 'ThemeDefaultDefault' in measure.json is textContent from display:none nodes. The accessible name is not doubled.

The link glyph stays aria-hidden, the chip gets no role or tabindex, and Change stays outside the summary.

The extra Tab stop is justified. WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard requires the fold to work from the keyboard, and one native summary is the minimum way to do that. The checked chip moves from the 3rd to the 4th Tab stop on a Default key, and from the 2nd to the 3rd on an explicit theme, where Change is hidden (MEASURED on the dial).

In B the focus order is summary, then Change, then chips. That matches the visual order (WCAG 2.4.3). Enter and Space toggle the band and are remembered. The focus ring is 2 px solid, drawn inside the row (MEASURED).
answers.q5_edge_states:
No reading (key): today the folded row shows the configured palette while the key draws its black prompt, and the help line that explains this is hidden (RD, shots1/B-key-empty-373-folded.png). AT02 puts that sentence on the row (46 px) and holds its slot, so the first reading moves nothing (MEASURED 0 px). A dial draws its prompt in its theme, so it needs no note.

Unknown stored theme: every variant shows no chip, and the row reads '"neon" (unknown; draws Void)' (31 to 41 px). That is honest, and the header face draws Void. I would not invent a swatch for a theme this version cannot draw. The long help sentence stays inside the band.

Paper shared theme: the light chip keeps its label-colored dashed frame and value-colored name, and reads clearly on the dark panel. Forced colors keep the palette, because .hw-theme-face has forced-color-adjust: none (MEASURED).

200% zoom (189 or 160 px wide, 205 px tall): the header fills the first screen and unpins, so the band always needs a scroll, in d04 too. MEASURED:
- No horizontal overflow in any state.
- No pick moves the chips at any width: 0 px across 8 themes, on keys and dials, on Void and Ultraviolet shared themes (lab3).
- No mid-word breaks.
- B and C open cost +16 px (233 vs 217), because 72 px stays reserved beside every line of the name, which wraps to 3 lines in a 60 px column.
- Folded: B 48 to 50 px, A 53 to 73 px, C 58 to 76 px (the chip on its own row).

keep: The band stays a details.hw-sec with id "sec-theme", open in the HTML, so it is open on the first open. Fold memory is unchanged: the id matches SECTION_ID and there are 10 section ids per panel, within the limit of 12.
Open all, Fold all and Alt-click include the band, and the folded row keeps the chip and the scope, so Fold all never hides the theme.
The band stays hidden until the fold answer arrives, like every other section. The palette cannot draw before the themes payload, which comes on the same plugin round trip (MEASURED).

Folded row is 'Theme [chip] (scope)'. The chip is a clone of the checked chip's face with its palette, the name on the face, Default's link mark and dashed frame, and the spark. For an unknown stored theme the row falls back to text: '"id" (unknown; draws X)'.
Change stays outside the summary as a sibling (never a control inside a disclosure button). It keeps its place, invisible, on an explicit pick.
The row never follows hover or focus. MEASURED: its words and chip are identical under hover of the row and of the chip, and under focus.
The chip updates in place when the shared theme changes from another panel, on a settings echo, on an unknown value and on a return to Default (MEASURED).
The name keeps its two reserved lines at zoom, and no pick moves the chips at any width (MEASURED 0 px).
The accessible name equals the visible words in every state, open and folded.
cleanup:
I stopped every process I started.

On Windows, cdp.mjs close() stops only the launcher it spawned. The real Chrome browser, a child of that launcher, keeps running and holds the debug port. Because of this, my first two runs leaked six browser trees on port 34052: browser PIDs 131024, 132236, 141372, 135164, 140796 and 131416. Each was a child of a launcher PID my runs printed (136636, 130200, 139656, 134512, 146408, 130972). I ended exactly those six with taskkill /T.

From then on, every lab ends with killmine.mjs. It ends only chrome.exe processes whose command line carries --remote-debugging-port=3405x.

Final check: no Chrome on ports 34050 to 34059, no listeners, and no node process from my directory.

The brief's measure.mjs and the other reviewers' labs probably leak the same way. I saw a lab browser on port 30082 that is not mine and left it alone.

I made no writes to the repository or the prototype directories. My scratch is C:\Users\stephen\AppData\Local\Temp\hw-tf-adversarial:
- lab1.mjs to lab7.mjs, killmine.mjs, lab2.log, lab3.json
- shots1, shots2, shots4 and shots7
- proto-B2 (AT01 and AT02 trial) and proto-A2 (the A Change-hit trial)
